title: The Ten Virgins
text:
Jesus compared the kingdom of heaven to ten young women who took their lamps and went out at night to meet a bridegroom and escort him to the wedding feast. Five of them were foolish and five were wise. The foolish ones took their lamps but no extra oil. The wise ones took flasks of oil along with their lamps.

The bridegroom was delayed. The hours went by, and all ten grew drowsy and fell asleep.

At midnight a cry went up: the bridegroom is coming, go out to meet him! The women woke and trimmed their lamps. The foolish ones found that theirs were going out, and they asked the wise ones to give them some oil. The wise refused: there might not be enough for both, they said. Better to go to the sellers and buy some for yourselves.

While the five foolish women were away buying oil, the bridegroom arrived. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut. Later the others came back and called out, asking to be let in. He answered that he did not know them. Jesus ended: keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour.
lesson: Expect delays and pack for them. Some kinds of preparation cannot be borrowed from others at the last minute, and the moment you are away scrambling may be the moment that matters.
location: Galilee and Judea (modern Israel and Palestinian territories)
